title: Kingdom of Hanover
capsule: The Kingdom of Hanover was constituted by the Congress of Vienna in October 1814, elevating the Electorate of Hanover to royal status under the British crown and placing it within the German Confederation as its fourth-largest member. It shared monarchs with Great Britain through the House of Hanover until 1837, when Queen Victoria's accession ended the personal union — semi-Salic succession law barred women from Hanover's throne while a male heir survived, so Ernest Augustus became king in his own right. During the Austro-Prussian War of 1866, Hanover's parliament voted to mobilize against Prussia; after its forces were defeated at Langensalza, Otto von Bismarck annexed the kingdom outright, incorporating it as the Prussian Province of Hanover by September 1866. George V, the last king, died in exile in Paris in 1878 without recovering his throne.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are precisely documented through German Confederation maps and Prussian annexation records; the kingdom's territorial extent is among the better-attested mid-nineteenth-century European states.
